summary: Iteration 14 — Twilio ConversationRelay streaming + Live Calls monitoring page + human takeover/hangup + voice_mode persistence. Backend: 9/9 pytest tests pass. Frontend: login works via Sign-in button click, sidebar nav-live-calls loads Live Calls page, voice-mode toggle persists (verified via reload) and Integrations partial-merge does not wipe other twilio fields.

integration_issues.issue: Could not exercise the takeover/hangup UI end-to-end because /api/calls/live/active returned an empty list at test time (the seeded 3cx active call did not match LIVE_STATUSES ∩ no-analysis filter, so no live-call card was rendered). The empty state renders correctly. Buttons are wired and dialog opens (verified via code + selectors), but a live card needs to appear for E2E click testing. Consider ensuring the seeded demo 3cx call has status='in_progress' (currently likely 'initiating' or similar not matching) or add one via the dialer.

action_items: Optional: seed a demo call with status='in_progress' and provider='twilio' (with a fake provider_call_sid) so the Live Calls UI has at least one card to click for E2E verification of takeover dialog + hangup toasts on the deployed preview.
Otherwise no action needed — all iteration-14 API contracts, guards, and Settings persistence are working.
critical_code_review_comments: conversation_relay.py: agent_reply is awaited (single reply, not streamed token-by-token). Twilio ConversationRelay client library sends the whole reply as one {type:text, last:true} — acceptable for now, but if user's 'sub-1s' goal requires per-token streaming, agent_reply would need to be refactored to yield tokens and send incremental messages before last:true.

routes.list_live_calls filter (LIVE_STATUSES + analysis:{$exists:false}) excludes calls whose provider text-cased status may not exactly match (e.g. Twilio returns 'in-progress' vs local 'in_progress'). Both forms are in LIVE_STATUSES so OK, but consider indexing status for scale.
routes.takeover_call / hangup_call use require_perm('leads','read') — reads permission for a destructive action. Consider a dedicated 'calls:takeover' capability.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (pages/wiring/persistence verified; UI takeover/hangup click flow gated by presence of an active live call — empty-state path verified)
